title: Nearby search by distance
description: Radius search for server apps: validated coordinates, haversine meters, a bounding-box prefilter that handles poles and the antimeridian, nearest-first keyset pagination, tenant and visibility scoping, location privacy with snapped cells and rounded distances, a PostgreSQL store without PostGIS and a Fetch adapter.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build, btoa/atob, TextDecoder and the Fetch Request/Response APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
Framework-neutral core; http.ts is optional. The SQL store needs plain PostgreSQL (no PostGIS or earthdistance).
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlNearbyStore with your query executor; elsewhere implement NearbyStore (atomic owner-checked upsert, bounding-box prefilter, exact distance, keyset order by distance then id).
Pass the signed-in viewer {tenantId, userId} from your session; never take the tenant from the request.
Choose each place's visibility: public (exact), approximate (others see a snapped cell and rounded distance) or private (owner only). Tune privacy.precisionMeters and distanceStepMeters.
Set maxRadiusMeters and maxLimit for your data density; for millions of rows in dense areas add PostGIS or earthdistance (see schema.sql).
Mount createNearbySearchHandler under one prefix with authenticate, allowedOrigins (cookie auth), a rateLimit hook, and routes/statusFor if your API shape differs.
limitations: Distances use a sphere (mean radius 6,371,008.8 m): up to about 0.5% from WGS 84 geodesics.
The SQL prefilter is a B-tree range on (tenant_id, lat, lng); it reads every row in the latitude band, so very dense or global datasets need PostGIS GiST or earthdistance.

Approximate places are filtered and ordered by their cell centre, so a place just inside the radius by its exact point can be excluded (and the reverse). Repeated radius probes can locate the cell, never the point inside it.
Rounded approximate distances can appear out of numeric order next to exact ones; order is by unrounded distance to the shared location. Cursors carry that unrounded cell distance.
Changing privacy.precisionMeters affects only places written afterwards; existing approximate rows keep their cells until updated.
The memory store is per-process; the SQL store is tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite, a single connection, not under real multi-connection contention or on every hosted Postgres.
Authentication, rate-limit storage, production query plans at your scale and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.
decisions: approximate places stored as a geohash cell centre; others' distances round up to the step
only the owner can update or delete a place (foreign id: forbidden on PUT, not-found on DELETE)
cursors bound to the exact center and radius; tenant from the viewer, never the request
options: routes, statusFor: override paths and statuses (default GET {prefix}/search, PUT|DELETE {prefix}/places/:id)

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/nearby-search.test.mjs tests/nearby-search-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: latitudes outside [-90, 90], longitudes outside [-180, 180], non-finite and non-number values fail with invalid-coordinates
haversine distances in meters match known vectors, including antipodes and the antimeridian
bounding boxes split at the antimeridian and open to all longitudes at the poles; a deterministic fuzz of 72,000 circle points finds none outside
radius search returns places nearest first with rounded meters and excludes places beyond the radius
keyset pagination by (distance, id) visits every place once, orders ties by id, survives inserts and rejects cursors from another query
searches across the antimeridian and at both poles find neighbours on the other side (memory and PGlite)
the memory store visits only covering geohash cells; on PostgreSQL the plan uses the (tenant_id, lat, lng) index and an exact distance check
other tenants never see places; private places reach only their owner; only the owner can update or delete, atomically under concurrent upserts
approximate places expose only a fixed snapped cell (or no coordinates) and distances rounded up to the step; the owner sees the exact point
HTTP adapter: 200 search with cursor, 201/200 PUT, 204 DELETE, 400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 429, bounded body and cache-control no-store
HTTP adapter: routes and statusFor overrides change paths and statuses

changes: First release: core, in-memory store, PostgreSQL schema and store, and Fetch adapter.
